newsitem.title: USA: Mead, IP to use natgas in Maine.
newsitem.headline: Mead, IP to use natgas in Maine.

text.p: Portland Natural Gas Transmission System said Tuesday two of Maine's largest paper mills have become the first there to agree to use natural gas.

The 26 million cubic feet per day to be transported to the Mead Corp paper plant Rumford and a cogeneration plant planned to serve International Paper Co's Jay plant brings long-term commitments for the Portland Natural system to 170 million cubic feet per day of firm transportation capacity.
This represents more than 95 percent of the expected initial throughput of Portland Natural's proposed 272-mile, $302 million pipeline.

The project is sponsored by subsidiaries of: Bay State Gas Co; Gaz Metropolitain and Co LP ; MCN Corp; El Paso Energy Corp; TransCanada PipeLines Ltd; and US Generating Co, owned by Pacific Gas and Electric Co and Bechtel Group Inc.

Portland Natural proposes to begin operations in November 1998 and will transport natural gas from an interconnection with TransCanada PipeLines near Pittsburg, N.H., to an interconnection with El Paso's Tennessee Gas Pipeline near Haverhill, Mass.

The cogeneration plant is proposed by Androscoggin Energy LLC, a company being formed by privately-owned Polsky Energy. In addition to providing steam for International Paper, it will generate electricity for sale on the open market, a Polsky spokesman said.
Portland Natural said it will transport natural gas to Rumford and Jay through a 43.5-mile ($34 million) lateral off its mainline. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
